comment.body:
Candidate rule proposed ## Reproduced symptom Reproduced — The gockowiak.pl homepage shows a first-party "Polityka prywatności" cookie-consent modal (`#cookie-modal1`) plus a Bootstrap `.modal-backdrop` that dims the whole storefront; the reporter-profile baseline confirmed both and no existing rule acted on them. A domain-scoped element-hiding rule `gockowiak.pl##.modal-backdrop, #cookie-modal1` verified in the A/B/C experiment (symptom resolved, page integrity intact, scroll preserved). ## Rule `gockowiak.pl##.modal-backdrop, #cookie-modal1` ## Executor and version Pinned prebuilt release v5.5.2.3 ## Policy rationale The report is a cookie/consent notice on a Polish shop, which is the stated purpose of the AdGuard Cookie Notices filter; it is not the site's own advertising, not a paywall, not a German anti-adblock wall, and not an anti-adblock wall of any kind (the page shows no detector and no request to disable the blocker). The instruction's policy rules that close a report (first-party ads, paywalls, German anti-adblock walls, non-reproducible reports) do not apply:⁠ the symptom was reproduced in the reporter-profile session and the fix fits the repository's Cookie Notices rules. Not a scam/phishing/malware page, so the special-case guidance does not apply either. ## Place in the list [AnnoyancesFilter/Cookies/sections/cookies_specific.txt](https://github.com/AdguardTeam/AdguardFilters/blob/25026a9205974e56aa63d22e43fe9868e89ffadc/AnnoyancesFilter/Cookies/sections/cookies_specific.txt) At the end of the file. ## Missing information - Traffic eligibility for gockowiak.pl under the filter policy's 100,000 visits/month criterion: The linked AdGuard filter policy requires a site to reach roughly 100,000 visits/month (public statistics or indirect indicators) before a site-specific rule is added. The run has no tool that returns traffic statistics for gockowiak.pl, so this criterion could not be checked; the proposal is made on the observed evidence and the maintainer decides traffic eligibility. ## Screenshots
Without and with the rule | Without the rule | With the rule | |---|---| | | |

issue.title: usnews.com
issue.body:
### Prerequisites - [x] This site DOES NOT contain sexually explicit material, otherwise use [NSFW-specific form](./new?template=bug_report_NSFW.yml); - [x] Filters were updated before reproducing an issue; - [x] AdGuard product version is up-to-date; - [x] Browser version is up-to-date; - [x] If the site or app is broken, disabling AdGuard protection resolves an issue. ### What product do you use? Other ad blocker ### AdGuard version wBlock 4.0.0 (Safari content blocker that uses and supports AdGuard filters) ### What type of problem have you encountered? Annoyances — pop-ups, cookie warnings, etc. ### Which browser(s) do you use? Safari ### Which device do you use? Desktop ### Where is the problem encountered? usnews.com ### Ad Blocking EasyList, AdGuard Base filter ### Privacy AdGuard URL Tracking filter, AdGuard Tracking Protection filter, Legitimate URL Shortener ### Social Widgets AdGuard Social Media filter ### Annoyances AdGuard Annoyances filter ### Security uBlock Origin – Badware risks ### Other _No response_ ### DNS filters _No response_ ### Language-specific _No response_ ### What Stealth Mode options do you have enabled? _No response_ ### Add your comment and screenshots 1. Subscribe to newsletter section on page annoyance. 2. Screenshots
Screenshot 1:
### Privacy - [x] I agree to follow this condition

comment.body:
Candidate rule proposed ## Reproduced symptom Reproduced — The reporter's annoyance is the inline "Newsletters" sign-up band on the usnews.com homepage, which stayed visible with the reporter's filters and that no existing rule covered. Adding `usnews.com###newsletters` to the Subscriptions section of the Annoyances filter hides exactly that block, and the bound review verified the symptom resolved with an intact page. ## Rule `usnews.com###newsletters` ## Executor and version Pinned prebuilt release v5.5.2.3 ## Policy rationale The reported defect is an on-page newsletter subscription annoyance, not first-party advertising, a paywall, or an anti-adblock wall, so none of the instruction's no-rule rules applies. The instruction's shared-rule guidance was checked:⁠ search_rules found no shared multi-domain rule for this element, and the site's own `#newsletters` id is site-specific, so a per-site rule in the file that already holds usnews.com subscription rules is the correct placement. ## Place in the list [AnnoyancesFilter/Popups/sections/subscriptions_specific.txt](https://github.com/AdguardTeam/AdguardFilters/blob/ef35cf812a4b2d1e7ba178006c92da5cbd16b124/AnnoyancesFilter/Popups/sections/subscriptions_specific.txt) At the end of the file. ## Screenshots
Without and with the rule | Without the rule | With the rule | |---|---| | | |
## Artifacts https://github.com/AdguardTeam/AdguardFilters/actions/runs/45096730268 Automated analysis against filters at `ef35cf8`. Posted by a filters agent; a maintainer reviews before anything is merged.

Indeterminate — The reported sticky "One gift. All of The Atlantic" subscription bar is a Zephr "gift-bar" campaign; on the reachable filtered baseline the same campaign appears as a 60px in-flow strip (div[⁠data-zephr-sdk-feature-slug="gift-bar"]⁠), but the reporter's fixed-bottom variant was never served and the unfiltered control stayed behind an HTTP 403 challenge, so no rule could be validated. Candidate for human review:⁠ theatlantic.com#⁠#⁠div[⁠data-zephr-sdk-feature-slug="gift-bar"]⁠ in AnnoyancesFilter/Popups/sections/subscriptions_specific.txt.

## Candidate for review

`theatlantic.com##div[data-zephr-sdk-feature-slug="gift-bar"]`

AnnoyancesFilter/Popups/sections/subscriptions_specific.txt

Not verified: No apply_rule phase ran. The reachable filtered baseline (AdGuard extension v5.5.2.3) served the same Zephr 'gift-bar' campaign as a 60px in-flow strip under the masthead (div[⁠data-zephr-sdk-feature-slug=gift-bar]⁠, outcome HOL26_G_GiftBar_General_MTD_Color_Blue, filled from www⁠.theatlantic.com/zephr/public/internal-templates/?ruleId=S-gift-bar-95), never as the reporter's fixed-bottom bar:⁠ no fixed/sticky bottom element, no 'One gift'/'Give a Subscription' text in the DOM, and scrolling to the page footer left the placeholder static. The unfiltered control could not be loaded (HTTP 403 Cloudflare 'Please hold a moment…' on all three attempts, technical_attempt_budget_exhausted), so the reported variant was never observed unfiltered and no before/after verification was possible. Risk if applied as-is:⁠ it hides the whole holiday gift-bar element in every placement; residue was not judged because the in-flow strip's height belongs to the hidden placeholder itself.

## Executor and version

Pinned prebuilt release v5.5.2.3

- Guidance for an unfiltered control that is HTTP 403-blocked while the filtered baseline loads: The reported target could not be loaded in an unfiltered control session (three navigations returned HTTP 403 with a Cloudflare 'Please hold a moment…' interstitial, ending in technical_attempt_budget_exhausted), while a prepared AdGuard-extension session loaded the same URL successfully. The run instruction and candidate rule policy say nothing about how far a run may go when the unfiltered control is unreachable but the filtered baseline is reachable, nor whether a prepared session may still be launched for apply_rule after the target's navigation budget is exhausted; the exhaustion guidance ('finish_fix with outcome=analysis_only') and the apply_rule validation requirement conflict here, so no candidate could be validated.

Analysis-only findings, no verified change

Fallback — Navigation timed out:⁠ Navigation did not complete after 1 attempt:⁠ https:⁠//cnn.com/ (page did not stabilize within 43145ms).

## Reproduced symptom

Indeterminate — On the loaded cnn.com homepage the right-hand sidebar reserves blank white space for empty ad slots — `.ad-slot[data-desktop-slot-id="ad_rect_atf_01"]` (294px, computed min-height 270px) plus `ad_nfs_btf_02` (144px), i.e. \~438px of empty right-rail space above the "CNN HEROES" module, matching the reporter's blank right-panel screenshots — so the candidate is `cnn.com##.ad-slot`. It stays unverified because every navigation to cnn.com with the AdGuard extension prepared timed out (page never stabilized), while the extension-free control loaded in \~4s, and the target's browser budget is now exhausted.

## Candidate for review

`cnn.com##.ad-slot`

BaseFilter/sections/specific.txt

Not verified: apply_rule never judged the candidate:⁠ phase B (filtered baseline) navigation to https:⁠//cnn.com/ failed with navigation_timeout ("page did not stabilize within 43568ms", 3 attempts), and the retry returned environment_capability_limited / phase_proof_unavailable (retryable:⁠ false); the target's browser-attempt budget is exhausted (3/3), so there is no filtered baseline, no phase proof and no visualReview verdict. Unfiltered DOM evidence supports the rule:⁠ sidebar `.ad-slot[data-desktop-slot-id="ad_rect_atf_01"]` keeps 294px (min-height 270px) and `ad_nfs_btf_02` keeps 144px of blank space with 0px creatives, i.e. \~438px of empty right-rail space above "CNN HEROES", matching the reporter's blank right-panel gaps.

## Missing information

- No documented route when the filtered page never reaches phase-proof stability: The run instruction (and the linked syntax/policy/contributing documents) say how to validate a candidate in the browser extension or AdGuard CLI, but say nothing about what to do when the filtering route itself stops the reported page from ever stabilizing:⁠ with the AdGuard extension v5.5.2.3 prepared on https:⁠//cnn.com/ (reporter's list set, then AdGuard Base filter only), every navigation and every apply_rule phase B attempt failed with navigation_timeout ("page did not stabilize within \~43s"), while the same URL loaded and settled in \~4s in the extension-free control session. The follow-up apply_rule call returned environment_capability_limited / phase_proof_unavailable (retryable:⁠ false) and the target's browser attempt budget (3/3) is now exhausted, so no filtered baseline and no phase proof exist. A stated fallback for this case (for example, how much unfiltered DOM evidence is sufficient to carry a candidate to human review) would have decided the outcome.

comment.body:
<!-- adguard-filters-agent:report {"schemaVersion":1,"revisionDigest":"eeac79eb6469003ab34577ecca45f8e11b6b0918ec6eaa505b873b021b80d388"} -->
Analysis-only findings, no verified change

## Reproduced symptom

Indeterminate — jackpoll.org opens an unsolicited "Keeping Jackpoll free isn't free" donation modal (25 s timer or \~60% scroll) that dims/blurs the page and locks it with body pointer-events:⁠none and overflow:⁠hidden. The site gates it on the localStorage key `jackpoll:support-prompt-seen`, so `jackpoll.org#%#//scriptlet('set-local-storage-item', 'jackpoll:support-prompt-seen', '1')` removed the popup and the page lock in validation runs, but the vision review kept rejecting on an unrelated self-animating hero preview card, leaving the rule browser-unverified.

## Candidate for review

`jackpoll.org#%#//scriptlet('set-local-storage-item', 'jackpoll:support-prompt-seen', '1')`

AnnoyancesFilter/Popups/sections/popups_specific.txt

Not verified: All three apply_rule runs resolved the reported symptom — the donation modal, its dimmed/blurred backdrop and the body pointer-events:⁠none / overflow:⁠hidden lock were gone, remainingInstances was empty and adLayoutResidue absent — but visualReview rejected each run for pageIntegrity 'regressed' on a single non-target element, the hero 'Customer feedback / Live preview' card, which it saw as an empty white panel. That card is the page's own self-animating preview widget:⁠ with the prompt dismissed in a live session (so the site's `jackpoll:support-prompt-seen` key is set, exactly the state the candidate creates) it rendered 'Question 2 of 4 · Rate your experience' and then 'Question 3 of 4 · How likely are you to recommend us? 0 10', and the same review settled three sibling demo panels (word cloud, live results, builder) as pre-existing blank regions. The harness cannot attach that measurement to a candidate refused for damage, so the rule stays browser-unverified.

## Executor and version

Pinned prebuilt release v5.5.2.3

## Artifacts

https://github.com/AdguardTeam/AdguardFilters/actions/runs/45097390680

Please block Ad-Shield advertisement by installing [tinyShield userscript](https://github.com/FilteringDev/tinyShield).

If you can understand Korean language, please refer https://github.com/FilteringDev/tinyShield/blob/main/README.ko.md.

New change of tinyShield's build script for Apple Safari Extension user is available.

## Still Have a Problem?
An issue is occurred when the userscript is applied, please report to [this issue tracker](https://github.com/FilteringDev/tinyShield/issues).

comment.body:
Candidate rule proposed ## Reproduced symptom Reproduced — Reporter-annotated floating "Make us a preferred source on Google" bar on www⁠.niagarafallsreview.ca is the shadow render of a first-party `` overlay, which the existing generic anchor-hiding rule cannot reach. A domain-scoped element-hiding rule `niagarafallsreview.ca##custom-tooltip[tooltip-id="preferred-source-google"]` was verified in the locked filtering session (symptom resolved, page integrity intact, no remaining instances, no residue). ## Rule `niagarafallsreview.ca##custom-tooltip[tooltip-id="preferred-source-google"]` ## Policy rationale The annotated target is a third-party-style self-promo/annoyance overlay (a 'preferred source on Google' prompt), not the site's own advertising, so the first-party-ad exclusion does not apply. It is not a paywall:⁠ the article and its lead photo are fully readable, no subscription wall is shown. It is not an anti-adblock wall:⁠ no page text asks to disable an ad blocker; the bar is a follow/preferred-source self-promotion prompt appearing with or without filtering. No policy rule in the run instruction closes this report (not a German anti-adblock wall, not scam/phishing), so rule generation is allowed. ## Place in the list [AnnoyancesFilter/Popups/sections/subscriptions_specific.txt](https://github.com/AdguardTeam/AdguardFilters/blob/1662e79b20cb4666beb9801266fe78cfec67ed9f/AnnoyancesFilter/Popups/sections/subscriptions_specific.txt) By adding the domain to the existing rule on [line 853](https://github.com/AdguardTeam/AdguardFilters/blob/1662e79b20cb4666beb9801266fe78cfec67ed9f/AnnoyancesFilter/Popups/sections/subscriptions_specific.txt#L853). ## Screenshots

Candidate rule proposed ## Reproduced symptom Reproduced — Reproduced the reported sticky footer on newsweek.com with the repo baseline loaded:⁠ a fixed, full-width beige "Membership" subscription drawer (Piano paywall drawer, top 954px / 126px tall, z-index 1000) covers the bottom of every page view. The domain-scoped element-hiding rule newsweek.com#⁠#⁠section[⁠class*="paywallDrawer"]⁠ was verified in the extension experiment (footer visible before, gone after, no remaining instances, page integrity intact); it belongs in AnnoyancesFilter/Popups/sections/subscriptions_specific.txt with the site's other subscription rules. ## Rule `newsweek.com##section[class*="paywallDrawer"]` ## Executor and version Pinned prebuilt release v5.5.2.3 ## Policy rationale Not the site's own advertising:⁠ this is a subscription/membership promotion footer, which the annoyance Subscriptions rules cover; the page's own advertising is untouched. Not a paywall gate the policy protects from circumvention:⁠ all page content stays visible behind the sticky footer, which carries a close X, and the candidate only hides the promotional drawer - it does not unlock or bypass paid content. No anti-adblock element:⁠ the page shows no ad-blocker detection message or wall, and no detector-driven overlay was observed, so the anti-adblock rules do not apply. Not a scam/phishing/malware report, so the 'handle it like any other' branch does not apply either. ## Place in the list [AnnoyancesFilter/Popups/sections/subscriptions_specific.txt](https://github.com/AdguardTeam/AdguardFilters/blob/6a591436f68243e16e0e8c1ac0f328c7a65d2c71/AnnoyancesFilter/Popups/sections/subscriptions_specific.txt) At the end of the file. ## Screenshots

comment.body:
<!-- adguard-filters-agent:report {"schemaVersion":1,"revisionDigest":"0a2489195d3334a5ff5f03e5393b698f2859012faa043241799b1fabbc2d295f"} -->
The filter policy leaves this report to a maintainer

## Reproduced symptom

The screenshot's defect is a dialog inside the native Android app 神盾測速照相 that asks the user to turn off VPN/private DNS/ad blockers after an ad request failed; the reported play.google.com URL is only the app's store listing, which loads cleanly with no overlay, no ad slot and no detector script in its 55 captured requests. Because the run instruction allows an anti-adblock rule only when the captured page requests show the detector script, and no environment here can run the app to capture them, this needs a maintainer's decision.

## Policy rationale

Run instruction, Filter policy:⁠ "Any other anti-adblock wall:⁠ write a rule only once the page's requests the agent captured show the detector script; without it, hand the report to a maintainer." — the requested detector script was never captured. The reporter-defined defect is a dialog drawn inside the native Android app tw.com.ainvest.outpack (神盾測速照相), not on the reported play.google.com page:⁠ full-page vision of the loaded reported URL returned reporterSymptomPresence "absent", pageObstruction "none", instanceCount 0, and the DOM contains no dialog and none of the dialog text (廣告請求未成功 / NETWORK_ERROR / 關閉後再試 / 廣告攔截 / VPN all false). The captured requests for the reported URL (55 requests, HAR artifact:⁠har:⁠dbb35dc7-badd-4406-a20d-60dddb43e2f9) contain no anti-adblock/ad-recovery detector host — only play.google.com and Google static/asset hosts, with the already-covered www⁠.google-analytics.com/analytics.js and www⁠.googletagmanager.com/gtm.js blocked by AdGuard Tracking Protection filter rules; inspect_ad_slots found 0 candidate ad containers. Restoring the ad-gated in-app feature (線上更新照相點) would mean unblocking the app's ad-SDK requests. A native Android app cannot be expressed in a $domain-scoped exception, so any unblock rule would be host-wide on an ad network, against the filter policy's quality requirements ("Unblocking rules must be as specific as possible to avoid unblocking anything unnecessary") and "it should not be unblocked if the blocking is caused by general filtering rules". The German anti-adblock exception does not apply:⁠ the page/app is Traditional-Chinese (zh_TW), so this is an "other anti-adblock" report and requires maintainer judgement. No rule can be validated:⁠ no available environment executes the native app, so no candidate could be verified; a maintainer must decide this app-side report.

## Missing information

- No route in the run instruction for anti-adblock reports whose symptom occurs inside a native Android app rather than a web page: The run instruction's anti-adblock rule requires that "the page's requests the agent captured show the detector script" before a rule may be written. Issue #⁠247885 is an AdGuard for Android report whose screenshot shows a dialog raised inside the native app tw.com.ainvest.outpack (神盾測速照相), while the reported URL is only that app's play.google.com listing. Neither locked environment (browser_extension, adguard_cli) can execute the native Android app or capture its traffic, so the app's ad-request/detector requests can never be captured, and the instruction says nothing about how such an app-side report should be evidenced or decided (only web pages are covered). I proceeded by capturing the reported URL's traffic and vision state, finding no detector script there.

## Artifacts

https://github.com/AdguardTeam/AdguardFilters/actions/runs/45111784655

<sub>Automated analysis against filters at `675eb32`. Posted by a filters agent; a maintainer reviews before anything is merged.</sub>

comment.body:
Candidate rule proposed ## Reproduced symptom Reproduced — bulgaronline.com shows a fixed Wix AI-assistant chat launcher ("Chat with Bulgarito") pinned over the bottom-right of the page, and the filtered baseline leaves it in place. The domain-scoped cosmetic rule bulgaronline.com#⁠#⁠[⁠data-hook="minimizedChat"]⁠ hid it in the browser-extension A/B/C experiment with page integrity intact and no remaining instances. ## Rule `bulgaronline.com##[data-hook="minimizedChat"]` ## Executor and version Pinned prebuilt release v5.5.2.3 ## Policy rationale The run instruction has no policy rule that closes this report:⁠ it is a chat-widget annoyance, not the site's own advertising, not a paywall, not a German anti-adblock wall and not an anti-adblock wall at all, so nothing blocks rule generation. The reported element is a chat launcher of the Wix AI assistant, which the AdGuard Widgets filter's purpose description explicitly covers ('Chat widgets that are not integrated with the content and are not the main content of the page'). The site's own promotional banners were left untouched; only the chat widget is hidden. ## Place in the list [AnnoyancesFilter/Widgets/sections/widgets.txt](https://github.com/AdguardTeam/AdguardFilters/blob/f6044931f16cd2fa485acd345fd00fda44555d40/AnnoyancesFilter/Widgets/sections/widgets.txt) At the end of the file. ## Screenshots
Without and with the rule | Without the rule | With the rule | |---|---| | | |

comment.body:
Candidate rule proposed ## Reproduced symptom Reproduced — The reporter's annoyance is the floating 'Feedback' chat-widget pill fixed at the bottom-right of msn.com; it is a first-party <⁠msn-feedback-link⁠> button inside two nested shadow roots, so no plain element-hiding rule can reach it and no list has a rule for it. A shadow-DOM scriptlet on the widget's button id was verified in the extension:⁠ the pill disappears, page integrity stays intact and no other content is harmed. ## Rule `msn.com#%#//scriptlet('hide-in-shadow-dom', '#feedback-link-button')` ## Executor and version Pinned prebuilt release v5.5.2.3 ## Policy rationale The report is a chat/feedback widget launcher, which the AdGuard Widgets filter policy covers ('Chat widgets that are not integrated with the content and are not the main content of the page'). It is not the site's own advertising, not a paywall, not an anti-adblock wall and not a scam/phishing page, so none of the run instruction's close-the-report rules applies. No existing rule or shared rule family covers this element (repo searches for its ids and classes returned no match), so a new site rule is the fix. ## Place in the list [AnnoyancesFilter/Widgets/sections/widgets.txt](https://github.com/AdguardTeam/AdguardFilters/blob/a317f8a9b0b5ef6a17cb0c0297f53bedde580ba1/AnnoyancesFilter/Widgets/sections/widgets.txt) At the end of the file. ## Screenshots

## Reproduced symptom

Indeterminate — On spoilerplus.sc the reader HTML carries 7 ad-slot containers (div[⁠data-cl-spot]⁠) plus an obfuscated inline ad loader, matching the reporter's in-reader ad, but in the AdGuard CLI baseline session no ad was ever requested or rendered and no popup could be provoked, so the candidate rule spoilerplus.sc#⁠#⁠div[⁠data-cl-spot]⁠ could not be visually verified. It is carried for human review, filed where Japanese site-specific hiding rules live.

## Candidate for review

`spoilerplus.sc##div[data-cl-spot]`

JapaneseFilter/sections/specific.txt

Not verified: apply_rule's bound visual review returned verdict 'inconclusive' with symptom 'unclear' (page integrity intact, remainingInstances empty, observedDamage empty, adLayoutResidue absent):⁠ the reporter's in-reader ad and the ad popups never manifested in either phase. In the filtered baseline the 7 div[⁠data-cl-spot]⁠ slots measured 0x0 and no ad-network request was issued, while the reader's own page images (img-cdn.stackpathcdn.app) got no response at all (status 0, no rule attributed by the CLI engine), so both captures show only a blank 'Loading.' reader field. The rule was applied in phase C (appliedRules:⁠ spoilerplus.sc#⁠#⁠div[⁠data-cl-spot]⁠) but there was no creative to remove and no visual change to confirm; a mobile-viewport session through the filtering proxy also could not rehearse the popups (no popup or tab from scroll/click).

The reported defect was not reproduced

## Reproduced symptom

Not reproduced — The reported "We see you're using an ad blocker" modal on the-sun.com did not appear in either an unfiltered control session or the AdGuard Browser Extension session loaded with the reporter's list family; the DOM holds no anti-adblock markup and the prepared page scrolls normally, while the repository already carries scriptlet fixes for this site's anti-adblock in AnnoyancesFilter/Popups/sections/antiadblock.txt. Recommend closing as not reproduced, noting that the reporter's wBlock Safari content blocker cannot execute those scriptlet rules.

## Executor and version

Pinned prebuilt release v5.5.2.3

## Policy rationale

The run instruction's filter policy closes reports for first-party advertising, paywalls, German anti-adblock walls, and it only permits a rule for any other anti-adblock wall once the captured requests show the detector script. None of those rules closes this report outright, so it stays open to rule generation (allow_rule_generation). This report is not being closed on a policy ground:⁠ it is closed because the reported defect could not be observed at all on the successfully loaded reported page, in either the unfiltered control or the prepared filtering session.

Indeterminate — On fifa.com a screen-filling self-promotion modal ("FIFA Women's Champions Cup Miami 2027™", BUY NOW) plus a dimming backdrop is loaded from the first-party request cxm-api.fifa.com/fifaplusweb/api/popup/…, and while it is open <⁠body⁠> is scroll-locked (ff-unscrollable, overflow hidden). Blocking that endpoint removed the popup with the page intact in the run's first experiment, but the domain-scoped literal the host requires was returned inconclusive on a page-integrity call whose "damage" is provably the page's own baseline skeleton placeholders, so the rule goes to a human unverified.

Candidate rule proposed ## Reproduced symptom Reproduced — givemesport.com leaves its social widgets visible — the article's "Like / Follow / Share" bar, the floating Like/Follow/Thread rail and the footer "FOLLOW US" icon row — because the site moved from `gms-` classes (still targeted by the stale `givemesport.com##.gms-share`) to generic `w-sharing` / `quick-action-sidebar` / `footer-social` markup. comment.body:
Candidate rule proposed ## Reproduced symptom Reproduced — On www⁠.flaschenland.de the Cookie Notices filter hides the shop's own consent banner (.cookie-permission-container), but the page's own CSS rule body:⁠has(div.cookie-permission-container[⁠style="display:⁠ block;"]⁠) keeps overflow:⁠hidden and paints a fixed rgba(0,0,0,0.5) :⁠:⁠before overlay, leaving the reporter a grey page with no consent buttons and no scrolling. A domain-scoped CSS rule that keeps the site's own consent bar visible while removing that leftover overlay and scroll lock was verified in the locked CLI-proxy baseline (symptom resolved, page integrity intact, no ad residue). ## Rule `flaschenland.de#$#body > div.cookie-permission-container[style^="display: block"], body:has(div.cookie-permission-container[style^="display: block"])::before, body:has(div.cookie-permission-container[style^="display: block"]) { display: block !important; overflow: visible !important; content: none !important; }` ## Policy rationale Run instruction:⁠ the site's own advertising, paywalls and German anti-adblock walls close without a rule. This is none of those:⁠ the page is broken by the Cookie Notices filter hiding the site's consent banner while the site's own consent CSS keeps its dim overlay and scroll lock — an incorrect-blocking defect. The page is not an anti-adblock wall:⁠ it shows no detection of the ad blocker and no request to disable it; it is a Shopware cookie-consent gate. Rule quality per filter policy:⁠ domain-scoped, no negative performance impact, restores the site's consent mechanism instead of unblocking ads (review:⁠ adLayoutResidue absent). ## Place in the list [AnnoyancesFilter/Cookies/sections/cookies_specific.txt](https://github.com/AdguardTeam/AdguardFilters/blob/1605ece4704dfc54c168a11fdef36c418be2d022/AnnoyancesFilter/Cookies/sections/cookies_specific.txt) At the end of the file. ## Missing information - Reporter settings import vs CLI-route evidence session: The issue carries a reporter settings import URL, and the run instruction's reporter-profile rules say that with an import URL only a session launched with settings kind "reported_on_current" may run apply_rule experiments. In the locked adguard_cli environment, a session launched with extension "prepared" plus settings "reported_on_current" (settingsVerified:⁠false) is refused by apply_rule with errorKind "cli_route_session_required" / requiredAction "launch_cli_evidence_browser", while the CLI-route evidence session (extension "none", which the environment's routing guidance prescribes) accepts no settings at all ("A control session (extension \⁠"none\⁠") runs no blocker and takes no settings"). The instruction does not say which session is authoritative for validation when the reporter settings import cannot be combined with the CLI evidence route, nor how to record the resulting baseline gap. ## Screenshots
Without and with the rule | Without the rule | With the rule | |---|---| | | |
## Artifacts https://github.com/AdguardTeam/AdguardFilters/actions/runs/45128243809 Automated analysis against filters at `1605ece`. Posted by a filters agent; a maintainer reviews before anything is merged.

comment.body:
Candidate rule proposed ## Reproduced symptom Reproduced — The element the reporter marked on the finans.mynet.com article is MyNet's own "Kredi Hesaplama Araçları" self-promo card in the right sidebar, still visible with the reporter's filter set because the existing mynet rule targets an older markup. The verified rule finans.mynet.com#⁠#⁠.sidebar-mymani-tools hides the card and leaves the page intact. ## Rule `finans.mynet.com##.sidebar-mymani-tools` ## Executor and version Pinned prebuilt release v5.5.2.3 ## Policy rationale No closing rule of the run instruction applies:⁠ the annotated card is not the site's own ad inventory — no mynetads/mynetreklam ad container or ad request renders it (get_network_log shows only first-party icon assets) — it is server-rendered self-promotion for mynet's own mymani.net tools, the rule kind the repository already keeps in AnnoyancesFilter/Other/sections/self-promo.txt. The report is not a paywall, not a German anti-adblock wall, and not an anti-adblock report at all. The repository already blocks this same mymani credit-widget family (mynet.com#⁠#⁠div[⁠data-fmymani-kredi-widget]⁠, mynet.com#⁠#⁠.mycredit-widget-container), so a domain-scoped element-hiding rule is permitted and precedented. The candidate verified with page integrity intact, no ad-layout residue and no observed damage, so no policy exception or human-review gate is triggered. ## Place in the list [AnnoyancesFilter/Other/sections/self-promo.txt](https://github.com/AdguardTeam/AdguardFilters/blob/94decfc6a8b943eaf43ad885501ee9a8bd0e228d/AnnoyancesFilter/Other/sections/self-promo.txt) At the end of the file. ## Screenshots

Not verified: The locked adguard_cli environment returned filter_selection_not_executable with filterBaseline {status:⁠ not_executable, code:⁠ filter_selection_missing}:⁠ the reported AdGuard DNS filter selection has no official baseline, so no candidate rule could be applied or observed in any phase and no live browser evidence was collected rather than substituting default lists. Independently, the reported flow is a native iOS app (Moises) whose in-app RudderStack SDK request cannot be reproduced in a browser session, and no network log from the reported apps.apple.com page was obtained to confirm the host is requested there.

## Missing information

- No executable baseline for AdGuard DNS filter selections, and no policy for trackers fired inside a native app: The locked adguard_cli environment answered with filterBaseline {status:⁠ not_executable, code:⁠ filter_selection_missing}, so the reported product's filter selection (AdGuard DNS Default server) has no official AdGuard baseline the run can validate against, and the run instruction gives no route for validating a rule for that selection. Also, the run instruction and its policy documents do not say how to treat a tracker report whose reporter field is a native mobile app ("Moises app") pointed at a store page:⁠ the repository cannot tell whether the intended target is the App Store web page's own requests or the app's in-app SDK traffic, and no document states whether an app-only tracker host should still get an unscoped network rule.

comment.body:
Candidate rule proposed ## Reproduced symptom Reproduced — keeplinks.org shows an "Ad blocker detected" anti-adblock modal (#⁠bn_box with its #⁠bn_bg backdrop) because the page's own inline detector probes the ad-path image /images/ads/banner_728-90.png, which the existing Base filter rule "_728-90." blocks, and checks a hidden bait div. The domain-scoped element-hiding rule keeplinks.org#⁠#⁠div#⁠bn_bg, div#⁠bn_box was verified in the reporter-profile session:⁠ modal gone, page content reachable, integrity intact. ## Rule `keeplinks.org##div#bn_bg, div#bn_box` ## Executor and version Pinned prebuilt release v5.5.2.3 ## Policy rationale The wall is not German (the page text is English), so the instruction's German-anti-adblock close rule does not apply. The run instruction allows a rule for any other anti-adblock wall once the page's captured requests show the detector script:⁠ the detector is a first-party inline script inside the captured document request (artifact:⁠har:⁠8b2bd71a-5b2d-4910-9751-3176209763ba), which builds the offscreen bait div and probes /images/ads/banner_728-90.png, and the applied Base filter rule "_728-90." makes that probe fail. The rule does not block the site's own advertising or a paywall:⁠ it hides only the anti-adblock overlay (#⁠bn_box and its #⁠bn_bg backdrop), leaving the first-party banner slot and the page's content untouched. Maintainer guidance prefers hiding the popup when that is enough; no scroll lock or blur persists, so no scriptlet is needed. ## Place in the list [BaseFilter/sections/antiadblock.txt](https://github.com/AdguardTeam/AdguardFilters/blob/a8e07ad54322d62b80d706d8821ffcd0a9a2c142/BaseFilter/sections/antiadblock.txt) At the end of the file. ## Screenshots
Without and with the rule | Without the rule | With the rule | |---|---| | | |
## Artifacts https://github.com/AdguardTeam/AdguardFilters/actions/runs/45138949380 Automated analysis against filters at `a8e07ad`. Posted by a filters agent; a maintainer reviews before anything is merged.

<!-- adguard-filters-agent:report {"schemaVersion":1,"revisionDigest":"faa9a8cdfd3be3a332099470b1fcf506653ebdb8a2ba3fa24fdb24e7d4a9dc74"} -->
Analysis-only findings, no verified change

## Reproduced symptom

Indeterminate — famitsu.com's mobile home page leaves three empty impact-ad containers (100px under the carousel, a 100px fixed bottom banner, 250px above the footer) whose loader the Japanese filter already blocks; a famitsu.com-scoped element-hiding rule hid all of them (probe:⁠ every targeted node 0x0, above-footer gap 250px→0, zero empty blocks left, page intact), but the bound vision review kept returning "not resolved" for blank space the DOM shows is the page's own spacing, so the rule stays browser-unverified.

## Still visible after the rule

- In-feed ad position between the block of six game banners (ファミキャリ！/GAMEPASS 完全攻略ガイド/THQ NORDIC/ファミ通40周年/あすかみずき PC紹介/DINOKUN) and the 「楽天ブラックフライデーでロジクール製品がセール中」 feature card — A centred grey 「広告」 label is rendered on its own line, followed by reserved white space with no delivered creative, divider or image inside the slot. The ad label/wrapper is visible, the ad content is not.
- TILE 4 — 動画, top of article feed — In the in-feed area at the top of TILE 4, a small 広告 label is visible at the right edge of the two-column feed row. The labelled ad position shows no delivered creative; only the residual label/ad slot is present.
- Between the top carousel/header block and the トピック / 新着記事 / 記事ラン... tab buttons — An empty reserved horizontal strip spans the viewport width below the carousel. No ad creative, 広告 label, frame, or placeholder block is visible in it; only blank space remains.

## Missing information

- No stated path for a candidate whose named residue is disproved by DOM checks but still reported "not resolved": The run instruction (AdguardFilters) and the terminal contract define exactly when an unverified candidate may be carried in analysis_only:⁠ an inconclusive review, an unreachable flow, an environment limit, or a residue-only rejection (adLayoutResidue present with symptom resolved/unclear, remainingInstances empty, pageIntegrity intact, observedDamage empty). This run hit a case none of those cover:⁠ apply_rule's structure probe measured every targeted empty ad container at 0x0 in the candidate phase, the domChecks measured a 250px above-footer gap reduced to 0 and zero remaining empty blocks anywhere on the page, pageIntegrity was intact and observedDamage empty — yet the bound visual review returned verdict rejected with symptom "not_resolved" plus remaining instances that are the page's own carousel/section spacing and 広告 label rows rather than ad residue. The instruction gives no criterion for whether such a candidate may be carried to a maintainer, and its explicit exclusion ("the symptom still there, remaining instances ... is not one to carry") forbids carrying it. It is also unclear whether the vision verdict or the DOM measurement governs when they disagree about whether a named blank space is ad residue. A rule for this disagreement (for example carrying the candidate with the structure/domCheck measurements as the unverifiedReason) is what this run lacked.

## Artifacts

I have added a few additional rules that should fix the issue (at least, everything works fine on my end with these rules and `Fanboy’s Annoyances` filter list enabled).

Please update your filter lists in about 3 hours (and make sure not to close the AdGuard app until the filter list update process is complete). Then, check whether the issue still occurs.

If it does, please try adding the following rule to your user rules:
```adblock
theverge.com#@%#//scriptlet('ubo-aeld', 'scroll')
```

comment.body:
<!-- adguard-filters-agent:report {"schemaVersion":1,"revisionDigest":"bb656861823f4775ef3e25552e26010e6447dde338c2c9038b67ef43114be86a"} -->
Analysis-only findings, no verified change

## Reproduced symptom

Indeterminate — Issue #⁠247916 reports that AdGuard DNS (device/router setup, Asahi Newspaper Viewer app) missed the tracker *.gcdsdk.appsflyersdk.com. No live verification was possible:⁠ the locked adguard_cli environment answered filter_selection_not_executable with filterBaseline code filter_selection_missing, so no baseline could filter the page or reproduce the leak. The repository already carries the host in SpywareFilter/sections/mobile.txt line 109, but as an unanchored 'gcdsdk.appsflyersdk.com^' rule while its sibling appsflyer endpoints use '||'-anchored rules; an anchored candidate is recorded for a maintainer.

## Candidate for review

`||gcdsdk.appsflyersdk.com^`

SpywareFilter/sections/mobile.txt

Not verified: The locked adguard_cli environment returned filter_selection_not_executable with filterBaseline code filter_selection_missing, so there was no baseline to load, no request to *.gcdsdk.appsflyersdk.com could be captured (the reporter's app cannot be driven), and apply_rule/lint could not run:⁠ the rule has no phase proof and no vision review. Additionally, an existing unanchored rule 'gcdsdk.appsflyersdk.com^' at SpywareFilter/sections/mobile.txt:⁠109 already substring-matches the reported wildcard host, so a maintainer should confirm whether the leak comes from that missing '||' anchor or from which repository files feed the AdGuard DNS filter before publishing an anchored rule beside the appsflyer group.

## Missing information

- No executable AdGuard DNS filter baseline (filter_selection_missing): Issue #⁠247916 is reported against AdGuard DNS (DNS setup:⁠ device or router), a network-resolver execution path. The run instruction routes reports to the built-in browser extension or to AdGuard CLI; no route reproduces a DNS resolver, and the locked adguard_cli environment answered filter_selection_not_executable with filterBaseline code filter_selection_missing (state capability_limited, skippedSources empty). So this run has no official baseline in which to capture a request to *.gcdsdk.appsflyersdk.com, no way to reproduce the reporter's leak, and no DNS-filter-specific guidance document:⁠ the served policy/placement documents describe the AdGuard DNS filter only as "used in AdGuard DNS. It is not a replacement for ad-blocking filters", without stating which repository filter files feed it or how a DNS-only leak should be evaluated.

## Artifacts

https://github.com/AdguardTeam/AdguardFilters/actions/runs/45157374853

issue.body:
### Issue URL (Incorrect Blocking) [https://www.nius.de/](https://adguardteam.github.io/AnonymousRedirect/redirect.html?url=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.nius.de%2F) ### Comment > On nius.de, readers with the "AdGuard Cookie Notices filter" enabled can no longer open or change their cookie consent. The filter blocks our consent management platform (Cookiebot), so the consent banner never loads and the footer link "Cookie-Einstellungen" only shows our fallback notice "Cookie-Einstellungen konnten nicht geladen werden". > > **Steps to reproduce** > 1. AdGuard for iOS 4.5.25 with "AdGuard Cookie Notices filter" enabled > 2. Open https://www.nius.de in Safari → no consent banner > 3. Tap "Cookie-Einstellungen" in the footer → the consent settings don't open, only our fallback notice appears > > **Expected:** users can always open the consent settings to give, change or withdraw their consent. The "AdGuard disabled" screenshot shows the Cookiebot settings dialog opened from the same footer link (desktop Chrome without AdGuard). > > **Request:** please add an exception so the Cookiebot consent dialog can be opened on nius.de via the footer link. ### Screenshots

comment.body:
Candidate rule proposed ## Reproduced symptom Reproduced — www⁠.arct.cloud shows a first-party fixed cookie-consent banner ("Cookies and data processing", Accept All / Only Necessary) across the bottom of every page. A domain-scoped element-hiding rule on the banner dialog alone — `arct.cloud##div[role="dialog"][class*="cookie-preferences-module"][data-brief]` — verified in the CLI filtering baseline:⁠ banner gone, page intact, full cookie-preferences panel still reachable. ## Rule `arct.cloud##div[role="dialog"][class*="cookie-preferences-module"][data-brief]` ## Policy rationale The run instruction's close-rules (paywalls; anti-adblock walls without a captured detector script; unreproduced ads) do not apply:⁠ the reported defect is a reproduced cookie-consent banner, which the AdGuard Cookie Notices filter exists to handle. The page's captured requests contain no ad-blocker detection script and no request to disable filtering, so this is a cookie-notice annoyance, not an anti-adblock wall; no third-party CMP host exists, so the site-specific Cookie Notices rule is the right instrument. Filter policy for the Cookie Notices filter:⁠ hiding the corresponding notice is the standard method when the site does not need a cookie decision for a feature to work; nothing on www⁠.arct.cloud was gated by the banner (content loads behind it, no consent cookie/storage key present before a decision). ## Place in the list [AnnoyancesFilter/Cookies/sections/cookies_specific.txt](https://github.com/AdguardTeam/AdguardFilters/blob/c74d5a750c74bc1de6db875475997199782a91cd/AnnoyancesFilter/Cookies/sections/cookies_specific.txt) At the end of the file. ## Screenshots
Without and with the rule | Without the rule | With the rule | |---|---| | | |
## Artifacts https://github.com/AdguardTeam/AdguardFilters/actions/runs/45176343330 Automated analysis against filters at `c74d5a7`. Posted by a filters agent; a maintainer reviews before anything is merged.

Candidate rule proposed ## Reproduced symptom Reproduced — prana24.pl shows a first-party cookie-consent modal ("Informacja o cookies") under a full-page dimming backdrop, and the reporter's AdGuard Cookie Notices list does not cover it. The single rule `prana24.pl##[id="cookies-message-modal"], .modal-backdrop` was verified in the reporter-profile browser extension session:⁠ modal and backdrop hidden, page undimmed and intact, scrolling preserved. ## Rule `prana24.pl##[id="cookies-message-modal"], .modal-backdrop` ## Executor and version Pinned prebuilt release v5.5.2.3 ## Policy rationale The report is a cookie notice on prana24.pl; the AdGuard Cookie Notices filter exists for exactly this, and no rule in the run instruction closes or hands off cookie-notice reports. It is not an anti-adblock wall:⁠ the live page showed no ad-blocker detection message, only the consent modal, so the anti-adblock evidence gate does not apply and no anti-adblock rule is proposed. It is not a paywall and not self-promotion, so neither the paywall close rule nor the self-promo placement rule applies. The candidate was fully validated (environmentExperiment verified, visualReview verified) in the locked reporter-profile browser-extension session, and the reporter baseline's complete full-page vision shows the reported symptom present. ## Place in the list [AnnoyancesFilter/Cookies/sections/cookies_specific.txt](https://github.com/AdguardTeam/AdguardFilters/blob/d5b905661988d22a80e29301ef2592fe83621cbf/AnnoyancesFilter/Cookies/sections/cookies_specific.txt) At the end of the file. ## Screenshots

comment.body:
Candidate rule proposed ## Reproduced symptom Reproduced — On school.yangcongxueyuan.com the AdGuard Tracking Protection rule `/webtrack.js` (filter 3) blocks the site's own tracker script fp.yangcong345.com/web-track-1.2.0/webTrack.js and the SPA then renders nothing at all — a completely blank white page with not even the site's login page. A narrow, site-pinned allowlist exception restores rendering (apply_rule verified, page integrity intact, no ads returned). ## Rule `@@||fp.yangcong345.com/web-track-1.2.0/webTrack.js$domain=school.yangcongxueyuan.com` ## Executor and version Pinned prebuilt release v5.5.2.3 ## Policy rationale The run instruction's filter policy states for tracking protection:⁠ 'Tracking protection filters should not block a tracker if blocking would disrupt the correct functioning of the website'; here blocking /webtrack.js left the reported page completely blank, and allowing it restored rendering. Quality requirement 'Unblocking rules must be as specific as possible':⁠ the candidate is an exact host + exact path scoped with $domain= to the reporting site only. The report is not a paywall, not an anti-adblock wall, and not self-promotion, so no policy rule closes it or hands it to a maintainer. ## Place in the list [SpywareFilter/sections/allowlist.txt](https://github.com/AdguardTeam/AdguardFilters/blob/4e2041662fa15f84c868288a544711df6a7a5072/SpywareFilter/sections/allowlist.txt) At its sorted position among the existing rules, before [line 4963](https://github.com/AdguardTeam/AdguardFilters/blob/4e2041662fa15f84c868288a544711df6a7a5072/SpywareFilter/sections/allowlist.txt#L4963). ## Screenshots
Without and with the rule | Without the rule | With the rule | |---|---| | | |
## Artifacts https://github.com/AdguardTeam/AdguardFilters/actions/runs/45183829267 Automated analysis against filters at `4e20416`. Posted by a filters agent; a maintainer reviews before anything is merged.

### Issue URL (Ads) [https://selcuksporthd.net/](https://adguardteam.github.io/AnonymousRedirect/redirect.html?url=https%3A%2F%2Fselcuksporthd.net%2F) ### Comment > Clicking Play opens a new tab to uplcm.com/4/12116931. The site calls window.open from its own script, so the ad URL can change. uplcm.com is not in any AdGuard list. With pop-ups blocked, the stream still plays normally. The domain may rotate (a number can be added, the TLD can change), so the site rule uses a regex domain. A scriptlet rule for the site itself will follow as a comment on the issue, because the form escapes quotes. > > Rules (form): > > ||uplcm.com^ > ||uplcm.com^$popup > > Scriptlet for the site itself. It blocks every pop-up on the site, so it keeps working if they switch to a different ad domain: > > [$domain=/selcuksporthd\d*\./]#%#//scriptlet('prevent-window-open') ``` Username: @vurijj ``` ### Screenshots

comment.body:
Candidate rule proposed ## Reproduced symptom Reproduced — kochboxcheck.de shows its own gd-consent WordPress plugin's cookie dialog ("Wir respektieren deine Privatsphäre") over a dimmed, blurred article, and no existing filter covers it. Blocking the first-party plugin script with ||kochboxcheck.de/wp-content/plugins/gd-consent/ removed the dialog with the page intact in the verified apply_rule experiment, filed in AnnoyancesFilter/Cookies/sections/cookies_specific.txt. ## Rule `||kochboxcheck.de/wp-content/plugins/gd-consent/` ## Policy rationale The report is a cookie-notice annoyance, which the AdGuard Cookie Notices filter exists to block ('blocks both cookie notices and requests from cookie management platforms'); the policy states that in most cases hiding or blocking the corresponding scripts is sufficient. It is not a paywall (no rule / recommend closing), not an anti-adblock wall (the page shows no detector demanding the ad blocker be disabled), and not a self-promotion placement handled by AnnoyancesFilter/Other/sections/self-promo.txt. No existing repository rule covers the site or the plugin (search_rules:⁠ 0 matches for kochboxcheck.de, gd-consent, .gdc-box, .gdc-backdrop), so a new rule rather than an extension of a shared family is required. ## Place in the list [AnnoyancesFilter/Cookies/sections/cookies_specific.txt](https://github.com/AdguardTeam/AdguardFilters/blob/dfacf5d3871d74cf4fefeb7c1161f0f13b323c12/AnnoyancesFilter/Cookies/sections/cookies_specific.txt) At the end of the file. ## Screenshots
Without and with the rule | Without the rule | With the rule | |---|---| | | |
## Artifacts https://github.com/AdguardTeam/AdguardFilters/actions/runs/45220984542 Automated analysis against filters at `dfacf5d`. Posted by a filters agent; a maintainer reviews before anything is merged.

comment.body:
Candidate rule proposed ## Reproduced symptom Reproduced — On www⁠.cozycozy.com/tr an app-install smart banner ("Uygulamayı indirin / daha iyi bir deneyim için", "Aç" CTA, X close, linking to cozycozy.go.link/app) sits above the logo and search form; it is rendered by the site's own Angular root component. Hiding the joli-phone-smartbanner element was verified in the AdGuard CLI proxy session:⁠ banner gone, page integrity intact, no residue, no remaining instances. ## Rule `cozycozy.com##joli-phone-smartbanner` ## Policy rationale The report is a mobile app-install banner, the exact category of the AdGuard Mobile App Banners annoyance filter, not a paywall, anti-adblock wall or product bug, so no policy rule closes it or hands it to a maintainer. The banner is dismissible, animated (slideUp trigger) and occupies a full-width strip at the top of the mobile viewport (\~74px of 812px) directly above the site's search form, so the filter policy's header/menu exception is considered and the element is blockable rather than protected. The remedy is a plain domain-scoped cosmetic rule in a shared list; no anti-adblock, consent or rewarded-ad gate is involved. ## Place in the list [AnnoyancesFilter/MobileApp/sections/mobile-app_specific.txt](https://github.com/AdguardTeam/AdguardFilters/blob/5882f9e5a19218e9e5af03359655c435fda43db2/AnnoyancesFilter/MobileApp/sections/mobile-app_specific.txt) At the end of the file. ## Screenshots
Without and with the rule | Without the rule | With the rule | |---|---| | | |
## Artifacts https://github.com/AdguardTeam/AdguardFilters/actions/runs/45219886845 Automated analysis against filters at `5882f9e`. Posted by a filters agent; a maintainer reviews before anything is merged.

Candidate rule proposed ## Reproduced symptom Reproduced — The "Wir verwenden Cookies" consent card on www⁠.rtl.de/tools/kochbox/gourmet/ is an orestbida-style cookieconsent dialog whose html classes also lock page scrolling, so plain hiding is insufficient; extending the existing shared remove-class scriptlet family with rtl.de removes the dialog and restores scrolling, and it verified in the browser experiment with the page otherwise intact. ## Rule `rtl.de#%#//scriptlet('remove-class', 'force--consent|show--consent', 'html')` ## Executor and version Pinned prebuilt release v5.5.2.3 ## Policy rationale Report is a cookie notice, which the repository's policy explicitly covers:⁠ the AdGuard Cookie Notices filter is built to block cookie notices and CMP requests (filter-policy.md, 'AdGuard Cookie Notices filter'). No run-instruction gate applies:⁠ it is not a paywall, not an anti-adblock wall, not a scam page, and not self-promotion. ## Place in the list [AnnoyancesFilter/Cookies/sections/cookies_specific.txt](https://github.com/AdguardTeam/AdguardFilters/blob/245ff59a235a00fce6da27d5bdc04fefe63e9f4a/AnnoyancesFilter/Cookies/sections/cookies_specific.txt) By adding the domain to the existing rule on [line 335](https://github.com/AdguardTeam/AdguardFilters/blob/245ff59a235a00fce6da27d5bdc04fefe63e9f4a/AnnoyancesFilter/Cookies/sections/cookies_specific.txt#L335). ## Missing information - Missing Safari "Script/scriptlet rules" section of the compatibility guidance: The compatibility topic of create-own-filters.md lists a heading "#⁠#⁠#⁠#⁠ Script/scriptlet rules" under SafariConverterLib, but every query I passed ("Script/scriptlet rules Safari", "scriptlets", "Cosmetic rules Safari limitations") returned only the neighbouring "Supported with limitations", "Not supported", "Cosmetic rules" and "Allowlist rules" sections. I could not retrieve whether `#%#//scriptlet(...)` rules work in AdGuard Mini for Mac / AdGuard for Safari, which matters because this report comes from AdGuard Mini for Mac v3.0.0 in Safari while verification ran in the Chromium AdGuard extension. The doc only states that scriptlet rules are not supported by AdGuard Mini for Android. ## Screenshots
Without and with the rule | Without the rule | With the rule | |---|---| | | |

Candidate rule proposed ## Reproduced symptom Reproduced — eurosender.com/pl still shows its "Cenimy Twoją prywatność." cookie-consent dialog with the reporter's Cookie Notices filter enabled, because the site now uses the self-hosted cookieconsent library (div#⁠cc-main) while the existing eurosender.com rule in cookies_specific.txt targets an older banner. Adding eurosender.com to the shared #⁠#⁠#⁠cc-main element-hiding rule hid the notice with the page intact. ## Rule `eurosender.com###cc-main` ## Executor and version Pinned prebuilt release v5.5.2.3 ## Policy rationale No rule in the run instruction closes this report:⁠ it is not a paywall, not an anti-adblock wall, and not a self-promotion case. The reported annoyance is the site's own cookie-consent notice, which is what the AdGuard Cookie Notices filter is for; the filter policy's Annoyance filters section covers cookie notices. The maintainer rule for popups/overlays prefers hiding when the page then works:⁠ after hiding, the page stayed intact, scrollable and with all its content (verified experiment). ## Place in the list [AnnoyancesFilter/Cookies/sections/cookies_specific.txt](https://github.com/AdguardTeam/AdguardFilters/blob/a404abe58eff1541db4bcf5e06c2e1366938ee75/AnnoyancesFilter/Cookies/sections/cookies_specific.txt) By adding the domain to the existing rule on [line 157](https://github.com/AdguardTeam/AdguardFilters/blob/a404abe58eff1541db4bcf5e06c2e1366938ee75/AnnoyancesFilter/Cookies/sections/cookies_specific.txt#L157). ## Screenshots

Analysis-only findings, no verified change

## Reproduced symptom

Indeterminate — The reporter's target is DLsite's own registration/coupon campaign strip at the very top of the product page (`.p-headerBannerPc`, first-party creative and first-party fetchHeaderBanner API), so the fix is the self-promo element-hiding rule `dlsite.com##.p-headerBannerPc`. DOM checks show it going from a rendered 40 px strip to `display:none` with the site header at y=0 and no gap or substitute band, but the vision review stayed inconclusive because the site's own Select Language overlay dims that region in every captured phase, so the candidate is carried to a human unverified.

## Candidate for review

`dlsite.com##.p-headerBannerPc`

AnnoyancesFilter/Other/sections/self-promo.txt

Not verified: No review confirmed it. DOM checks on the locked baseline measured it as intended (rendered 40 px at y=0 -⁠> display:⁠none, height 0; site <⁠header⁠> moves to y=0 at unchanged 91 px; .floor-nav-scroll identical in both phases; only wrappers and header rows in the top 45 px), but the vision review ended inconclusive (symptom unclear, remainingInstances empty, adLayoutResidue absent, observedDamage empty, pageIntegrity unclear) because the site's own Select Language / adult-check overlay and its dimmed backdrop cover the top band in every captured phase; the reporter's cookies had already answered that overlay, so they saw no such mask. Its earlier rejections named the site's persistent navigation rows (.l-header__core-sub / .floor-nav-scroll), which the checks show are byte-identical before and after the rule. The candidate's three allowed runs are spent and the overlay-dismissal rehearsal is refused in every phase.

comment.body:
Candidate rule proposed ## Reproduced symptom Reproduced — On www⁠.urawa-keiba.jp news detail pages the "この記事をシェアする" share panel is left as an empty pale-blue box:⁠ the social filter already hides its X/LINE/Facebook share links (all three anchors compute display:⁠none) but the container and heading still render. Hiding the container with `urawa-keiba.jp##.c-article__share-box` was verified in the AdGuard CLI filtering baseline — the panel is gone, nothing else changes and page integrity stays intact. ## Rule `urawa-keiba.jp##.c-article__share-box` ## Policy rationale The report is a social-widget report; the run instruction's closing rules (paywalls, anti-adblock without a captured detector script, scam pages) do not apply, and the page requests no anti-adblock detector. AdGuard filter policy states the AdGuard Social Media filter blocks social media widgets such as Like and Share buttons on third-party sites; the reported panel is a share-button widget, not site functionality or a link to the site's own social pages (the footer social-page links are left untouched). ## Place in the list [SocialFilter/sections/specific.txt](https://github.com/AdguardTeam/AdguardFilters/blob/245ff59a235a00fce6da27d5bdc04fefe63e9f4a/SocialFilter/sections/specific.txt) At the end of the file. ## Screenshots

Candidate rule proposed ## Reproduced symptom Reproduced — remotecanteen.com/prepmymeal/ shows a Real Cookie Banner 5.4.3 "Privatsphäre-Einstellungen" dialog that covers the article and locks scrolling; the site's existing trusted-click-element rule is applied but does not dismiss it, and hiding the wrapper alone leaves html/body with overflow:⁠hidden. I propose a domain-scoped CSS rule that moves the fixed consent layer (wrapper plus its dialog) off-screen and releases the scroll lock, verified by apply_rule with the symptom resolved and page integrity intact. ## Rule `remotecanteen.com#$#html, body, div[consent-skip-blocker="1"], div[consent-skip-blocker="1"] dialog { overflow: visible !important; top: 100000px !important; }` ## Executor and version Pinned prebuilt release v5.5.2.3 ## Policy rationale The report is a cookie-consent notice (label 'T:⁠ Annoyance', comment 'cookie') on remotecanteen.com/prepmymeal/, reproduced live:⁠ a Real Cookie Banner 5.4.3 dialog 'Privatsphäre-Einstellungen' over the article with a scroll lock. None of the run instruction's closing rules applies:⁠ this is not a paywall, not an anti-adblock wall (the page shows no ad-blocker detector request or message), and not a self-promotion or other-party ad case. The fix belongs to the repository's Cookie Notices filter, where this site already has a (non-working) rule, so rule generation is allowed. ## Place in the list [AnnoyancesFilter/Cookies/sections/cookies_specific.txt](https://github.com/AdguardTeam/AdguardFilters/blob/a404abe58eff1541db4bcf5e06c2e1366938ee75/AnnoyancesFilter/Cookies/sections/cookies_specific.txt) At the end of the file. ## Screenshots

Analysis-only findings, no verified change

## Reproduced symptom

Indeterminate — kochboxguru.de serves a full-viewport "Privatsphäre-Einstellungen" consent modal (Real Cookie Banner Pro 4.4.1) that also sets inline overflow:⁠hidden on html/body, so hiding it with CSS would leave the article unscrollable. Clicking its decline button ("Weiter ohne Einwilligung") removes the dialog and the scroll lock; the trusted-click-element rule was applied in the experiment but the bound vision review read a pre-render consent scrim as a still-present gate, so validation stayed inconclusive and the rule is carried for human review.

## Candidate for review

`kochboxguru.de#%#//scriptlet('trusted-click-element', 'dialog a[role="button"][data-order="1"]')`

AnnoyancesFilter/Cookies/sections/cookies_specific.txt

Not verified: apply_rule applied the scriptlet (status "applied") and phase C shows the dialog gone, the inline overflow lock on html/body cleared, no full-viewport overlay, and the original-resolution phase C tile free of any consent panel or scrim at normal contrast; but the bound vision review returned "rejected"/symptom not_resolved from the phase C viewport artifact, which shows only the consent scrim captured before the panel renders (the baseline viewport artifact shows the same scrim with no panel), so environmentExperiment stayed inconclusive. Live interact_page rehearsal of the same click removed the dialog and the scroll lock, proving the mechanism; remainingCandidateAttempts fell to 1 with no semantically distinct broader selector for this gate.

Pinned prebuilt release v5.5.2.3

comment.body:
Candidate rule proposed ## Reproduced symptom Reproduced — hamal.co.il pins a full-width Hebrew cookie notice (div[⁠aria-label="הודעה על שימוש בעוגיות"]⁠) over its feed, and the repo already hides the identical element on walla.co.il. The domain-scoped rule proposed here verified in the A/B/C experiment (notice gone, page intact) and the host merges it into that existing Cookie Notices rule. ## Rule `hamal.co.il##div[aria-label="הודעה על שימוש בעוגיות"]` ## Executor and version Pinned prebuilt release v5.5.2.3 ## Policy rationale The report is an ordinary cookie notice; blocking cookie notices is the stated purpose of the AdGuard Cookie Notices filter, so no run-instruction rule closes it. No paywall, no anti-adblock wall, no self-promotion and no dangerous page is involved:⁠ the reported symptom is a consent bar rendered by the site's own scripts. The fix extends an existing rule with the same expression (walla.co.il#⁠#⁠div[⁠aria-label="הודעה על שימוש בעוגיות"]⁠) rather than adding a duplicate, as the repository's placement guidance and the maintenance rule about shared rules require; the proposed line is the reported domain scoped alone, which the host merges into that existing rule. ## Place in the list [AnnoyancesFilter/Cookies/sections/cookies_specific.txt](https://github.com/AdguardTeam/AdguardFilters/blob/5d2f981f6c339f2b32107076790145e0557ecf64/AnnoyancesFilter/Cookies/sections/cookies_specific.txt) At the end of the file. ## Screenshots

<!-- adguard-filters-agent:report {"schemaVersion":1,"revisionDigest":"55752d15af022553c717be6dd98ffe3a9bc97107ed38818ad153e21b1d93ea9c"} -->
Analysis-only findings, no verified change

Fallback — The page refused to load in the run browser:⁠ main document returned HTTP 429

## Reproduced symptom

Indeterminate — Report asks to hide the cookie consent notice on tv10.co.il. Live verification was impossible:⁠ all three navigation attempts to the reported URL returned HTTP 429 with a "Vercel Security Checkpoint" page, exhausting the attempt budget, so no DOM or visual evidence could be collected. The unverified candidate `tv10.co.il##section[aria-label="הסכמה לשימוש בעוגיות"]` is handed to a maintainer, to be filed in AnnoyancesFilter/Cookies/sections/cookies_specific.txt where site-specific cookie rules live; no existing rule covers this domain.

## Candidate for review

`tv10.co.il##section[aria-label="הסכמה לשימוש בעוגיות"]`

AnnoyancesFilter/Cookies/sections/cookies_specific.txt

Not verified: Browser access never succeeded, so `apply_rule` could not be run:⁠ three navigation attempts to https:⁠//tv10.co.il/ (desktop/he-IL/untouched, desktop/en-US/accept, mobile/he-IL/reject, all with the AdGuard Cookie Notices filter as baseline) each returned HTTP 429 with the page title "Vercel Security Checkpoint", and the third attempt returned technical_attempt_budget_exhausted. There is therefore no DOM, network-log or screenshot evidence that the element selected by the reporter exists, that hiding it leaves no layout gap, or that the page stays scrollable; a possible bot/security checkpoint is an unverified hypothesis. The rule is the reporter's own content-specific selector and is unconfirmed; repository inventory shows no existing cosmetic or network rule for tv10.co.il, so it duplicates nothing, and without a network log no CMP/vendor request could be identified to justify a `||vendor^$domain=` rule instead.

Pinned prebuilt release v5.5.2.3

Candidate rule proposed ## Reproduced symptom Reproduced — The prepared AdGuard Browser Extension reproduces the report on www⁠.hackingwithswift.com/100/swiftui/:⁠ a fixed black "BLACK FRIDAY SALE:⁠ Save 50% on my books and bundles!" bar sits under the header (the reporter's "sticky header advertising sale"), while the annotated in-content promo card of the same sale is already hidden by the existing hackingwithswift.com#⁠#⁠.hws-sponsor rule. The candidate hackingwithswift.com#⁠#⁠skybar#⁠hws-latest-tutorial was verified by apply_rule — bar visible before, hidden after, page integrity intact, no residue, no remaining instances — and belongs in AnnoyancesFilter/Other/sections/self-promo.txt. ## Rule `hackingwithswift.com##skybar#hws-latest-tutorial` ## Executor and version Pinned prebuilt release v5.5.2.3 ## Policy rationale The run instruction's filter policy says self-promotion — page elements where the site promotes its own products and services with no third party paying — gets a rule proposed for AnnoyancesFilter/Other/sections/self-promo.txt, and that whether it is annoying enough to block is the maintainer's call, so this report is open to rule generation. The bar promotes the site's own Black Friday sale of the author's books/bundles on its own /offers page; no third-party advertiser is involved, so it is self-promotion rather than an ad, and it is not a paywall, an anti-adblock wall, or a dangerous page that the other policy rules would close or hand off. ## Place in the list [AnnoyancesFilter/Other/sections/self-promo.txt](https://github.com/AdguardTeam/AdguardFilters/blob/5d2f981f6c339f2b32107076790145e0557ecf64/AnnoyancesFilter/Other/sections/self-promo.txt) At the end of the file. ## Screenshots

comment.body:
<!-- adguard-filters-agent:report {"schemaVersion":1,"revisionDigest":"2d5b47aff2144913e942d9efa2d593a05181a27f6fd81b9d120090a554d5d90b"} -->
The filter policy leaves this report to a maintainer

## Reproduced symptom

The two "trackers" reported on z2u.com's login page are the site's own NetEase Yidun captcha/anti-fraud backend:⁠ c.dun.163.com serves the NECaptcha config/token for captchaId 3f96045c46e849b4983242fb0288815a that the login form's NECaptchaValidate field depends on. AdGuard's filter policy excludes anti-bot/fraud protection from tracking-protection blocking, so no rule is proposed and a maintainer should confirm closing.

## Policy rationale

Filter policy (KnowledgeBase filter-policy.md, 'Tracking protection filters → Limitations and exceptions', served by lookup_rule_guidance):⁠ tracking protection filters should not block a tracker if blocking would disrupt the correct functioning of the website — 'Anti-bots and fraud protection if it interferes with using the site. For example, with PerimeterX or hCaptcha blocking causes problems when the site attempts to verify its visitor with a captcha'. The two reported requests are that anti-bot/fraud-protection backend, not behavioural analytics:⁠ c.dun.163.com is the NetEase Yidun risk-control/captcha endpoint the page's own login uses (captchaId 3f96045c46e849b4983242fb0288815a in both the reporter's collect URL and the page's inline initNECaptcha call), and nstool.netease.com belongs to the same NetEase risk SDK. Live evidence on the reported page:⁠ c.dun.163.com/api/v2/getconf and the cstaticdun.126.net captcha SDK load on https:⁠//www⁠.z2u.com/login.html, the form carries a hidden input name="NECaptchaValidate", and the onVerify handler is what appends captcha_validate to #⁠login_form — a host-level rule such as ||c.dun.163.com^ would remove the login captcha's backend. The interference clause is conditional and the post-submit requests could not be rehearsed (interact_page refused credential typing/sign-in as unsafe), so a maintainer should confirm the recommendation rather than the run asserting a verified policy outcome; a host-level rule would also affect every other site using Yidun captchas (no existing ||c.dun.163.com or ||nstool.netease.com rule exists in this repository).

comment.body:
<!-- adguard-filters-agent:report {"schemaVersion":1,"revisionDigest":"1177e4f0ec54308f2efe37288cc92d6ff5509d57d8e705450a383dacfb941c22"} -->
The filter policy recommends closing without a rule

## Reproduced symptom

The reported wall on golgebahcesi.com is a genuine ad-blocker detection notice (it appears only with filtering on and the page pings its own /api/notices/rk/detected), but its own "Şimdilik devam et" button dismisses it, the page stays usable, and the dismissal is remembered in localStorage. The filter policy does not block detection messages that let the user proceed to the content, and no detector script request exists in the captured HAR, so I recommend closing without a rule for a maintainer to confirm.

## Executor and version

Pinned prebuilt release v5.5.2.3

## Policy rationale

Filter policy (KnowledgeBase filter-policy.md, 'Ad blocking filters' → 'Limitations and exceptions'):⁠ "We do not block ad blocker detection messages that satisfy at least one of the following criteria:⁠ ... They allow the user to proceed to the website's content." Verified live:⁠ the muted 'Şimdilik devam et' button removed the full-viewport overlay (interact_page obstructionDelta -1), the page stayed usable and scrollable (document height 7849), localStorage key site_notice_rk_seen was set to "1", and a reload afterwards rendered no overlay. Same policy passage:⁠ "They provide an alternative to disabling an ad blocker given that this alternative does not put the users' privacy or security at risk" — the notice offers an ad-free VIP path ('VIP ol, reklamsız oku' → /vip) beside the instructions to disable the blocker. Run instruction, anti-adblock walls:⁠ "write a rule only once the page's requests the agent captured show the detector script; without it, hand the report to a maintainer." No detector script appears in the captured HAR:⁠ detection runs inside the site's own first-party Next.js chunks (/_next/static/chunks/*.js) and is reported to first-party endpoints /api/notices/rk/checked and /api/notices/rk/detected, so there is no identifiable detector resource to neutralize and the decision belongs to a maintainer. Run instruction policy:⁠ paywalls get no rule; part of this notice is an upsell to the site's ad-free VIP subscription, which speaks against blocking it.

## Artifacts

https://github.com/AdguardTeam/AdguardFilters/actions/runs/45291522736
